On October 15, 1794, the Philadelphia Mint delivered 1,758 silver dollars, struck on a hand-turned screw press. It was the only day of dollar production that year.

These Flowing Hair dollars were the first silver dollars issued by the United States. Fewer than 200 are believed to survive.

The finest known example is unusual. A small silver plug was added to its blank at the Mint to bring it up to standard weight, and some experts believe it may be the very first silver dollar struck.

In 1947 the coin changed hands for $1,250. On January 24, 2013, at a Stack's Bowers Galleries auction in New York, it sold for $10,016,875. It was the first coin ever to top $10 million at auction.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Twenty human rights organizations have called for the release of detainees and the dropping of charges related to peaceful religious activities in Bahrain, expressing concern over the mass trial of Shia clerics and allegations of torture and forced confessions.

Amnesty International and 19 other human rights organizations have issued a joint statement expressing concern over the mass trial of Shia clerics in Bahrain, warning of allegations of torture, ill-treatment, forced confessions, and violations of fair trial standards, according to a report by Alahed News on Wednesday.
​
The proceedings involve 69 defendants, including 60 Shia clerics and nine affiliates, the statement said, adding that of the 56 defendants in custody, 47 are clerics, and nine are affiliates; the remaining 13 clerics are being tried in absentia.
​
The signatory organizations, citing reports of detention at undisclosed locations, denial of access to lawyers, threats against defendants and their families, and pressure to sign confessions, called for an independent investigation into torture allegations and the exclusion of confessions obtained under duress.
​
The organizations also urged Bahraini authorities to uphold fair trial standards, ensure defendants have access to legal counsel and case documents, immediately release those arbitrarily detained, and drop charges related to peaceful religious activities.
​
On Monday, scores of Bahrainis, mostly Shia clerics according to a rights group, were sentenced to life in prison over what authorities described as undermining the state.
​
